name: The Tuller household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: tuller_elam

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-01-28, 27 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

arrival_year.note: A STATED YEAR, WHERE THE FIELD HELD A DRAW. The same county biography says the family of tuller_elam reached Chicago in July 1833. The year drawn by the arrival stage read 1833 as well, so the value does not move — what moves is that it is now a reading with a source behind it rather than a figure taken from a distribution. The MONTH is stated by the source and is not written into this field, which carries a year; the household's own `arrival` block holds its separate bound of 1834-01-01 from the Chicago Democrat and is untouched, because a bound and an arrival are two claims. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source earlier than 1 July 1835 corroborates and dates and never promotes: the person's grade does not move on this.

origin.note: A SOURCE, WHERE THE FIELD HELD A DRAW. The completed resident-research pass on tuller_elam read a county biography as saying that Elam Tuller's family reached Chicago in July 1833 and as identifying his Connecticut origin and his farmer, mechanic and steam-engine manufacturing background. The block this replaces read “The Mid-Atlantic states”, drawn from the Old Settlers birthplace sample and resting on nothing about this household.

reason_for_coming.value: The 1834 season: the harbour works, the opening of the bar and the trade that followed them
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `letter_list_returns` as `1834-04-16`, which reaches 1834-04-16 — 441 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. A RETURN IS A DATE AND NOT A CITATION: `letter_list_returns` carries no source per return, so this leg cites none and the corpus that printed it is named in the person's own `sources`. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1834-04-16 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, AND HELD THERE MORE THAN ONCE. The papers print 'Elam Tuller' and 'nin 2 Elam Tuller meron' in 2 separate returns of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 28 January 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 16 April 1834, column 17 — across 1834-01-28 to 1834-04-16. A name in a LATER return is somebody still being written to, months on, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is why this person outranks a single-return name of the same surname. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.evidence_for: A county biography says Elam Tuller's family reached Chicago in July 1833 and identifies his Connecticut origin and farmer, mechanic and steam-engine manufacturing background. Two letter returns support the chronology.
resident_research.notes: Candidate facts remain unasserted until a source bridges the candidate to the historical record by more than name similarity.
resident_research.summary: Carried forward from pass 2, which read the Whiteside County biography and never completed a ledger: it puts the Tuller family in Chicago in July 1833 and gives the Connecticut origin and the farmer, mechanic and steam-engine manufacturing background. Two letter returns support the chronology. The arrival is the biography's, and is carried as such.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'tuller_elam:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 30 under 40', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('tuller_elam:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
